extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students and researchers interested in comedy genres
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and describe the defining characteristics, mechanisms, and typical formats/works of the cringe comedy subgenre of comedy (film/television).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Derives humor from social awkwardness, guilty pleasure, self-deprecation, idiosyncratic humor, and personal distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article explicitly lists these affective and social sources as what the subgenre draws on; use of these elements in scenes, dialogue, and character situations is indicative of cringe comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pseudo-reality / mockumentary form
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of cringe comedy are pseudo-reality TV shows, sometimes with an air of a mockumentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cringe comedies often adopt documentary-like presentation or pseudo-reality techniques to lend authenticity; producers may place actors in apparently 'real' settings to heighten discomfort and the sense that awkwardness is happening 'for real.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious, verisimilar settings (e.g., workplace)
rubrics_metrics.description: They revolve around a serious setting, such as a workplace, to lend the comedy a sense of reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing absurd or awkward behaviour in otherwise normal/serious contexts increases the incongruity and audience discomfort; choosing realistic, everyday environments is a common production/creative choice for the genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protagonist character type: egotists who break norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, the protagonists are egotists who overstep the boundaries of political correctness and break social norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterization of leads as self-centered, tone-deaf, or boundary-violating is a hallmark; these traits create situations that generate cringe when interacting with others and social expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic mechanism: denial/obliviousness to ego-deflation
rubrics_metrics.description: The comedy will attack the protagonist by not letting them become aware of their self-centered view, or by making them oblivious to the ego-deflation that the comedy deals them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humour arises from the protagonist's lack of self-awareness and the audience's superior knowledge; crafting scenes where the character remains unaware of their humiliation is a core technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of moral expectations (lack of consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes an unlikable protagonist may not suffer any consequences, which violates people's moral expectations, and also makes the audience cringe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subverting the expected moral payoff (i.e., failing to punish or humble the offending character) can intensify discomfort and the cringe response; this is a deliberate narrative choice in some works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience response mechanism: incongruity and annoyance interplay
rubrics_metrics.description: Explained via incongruity theory and annoyance (Noël Carroll): whether a person finds an incongruous deviation amusing depends on their disposition; one cannot be both genuinely amused and genuinely annoyed by the same deviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The genre relies on balancing incongruity (recognizable deviation from norm) with viewer tolerance for annoyance; creators must calibrate situations so some viewers perceive the deviation as comic rather than merely irritating—the cutlery example illustrates this audience-sensitivity dynamic.
